name_reason: Name follows the game-global convention data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> and accurately reflects both purpose and data type: domain 'chapter'; 'ch18' is a meaningful chapter ID (valid range 01-30, not an address residue); 'end_scene' is the access context; 'char_pos_y' is the per-character Y-coordinate meaning; 'table' encodes the array/table data type. No Ghidra address residue in the name (it does not contain hex tied to 0x521d4 or any data address). The '18' is a domain ID and 'y' is a coordinate axis -- both semantic, must be kept.
purpose: Per-character Y tile coordinate table for the chapter 18 (Distant Shore / 遙遠的彼岸) end scene; supplies the pos_y placement bytes when the chapter 18 end handler sets up characters and camera.
logic_summary: fd2_chapter_18_end copies all 17 bytes onto the stack (MOVSD x4 + MOVSB at 0x23D03/0x23D05, source 0x521D4) and passes the block as the pos_y argument to fd2_setup_chars_and_camera_for_intro. That consumer indexes the block by char index (runtime_char[char_idx].bPos_y = pos_y_base[char_idx]), reading one byte per character (stride 1), and stores it into runtime_char.bPos_y. The table sits between the pos_x_table (0x521C3, preceding) and the facing_table (0x521E5, following) -- the three adjacent MOVSD copy sources in the handler bound this table at 17 bytes.
element_semantics: Each byte = the battlefield Y tile coordinate for one character slot in the chapter 18 end-scene arrangement (values observed 5..10). Indexed by char index in the handler's placement loop. Note the handler only places chars 0x10..0x11 (loop range) plus additional char indices, so not all 17 entries are necessarily consumed by char index, but the block is copied whole; entries [10..16] = {5,5,5,10,10,10,7}.
notes: Verified: src data values {7,8,6,7,8,9,6,7,8,9,5,5,5,10,10,10,7} byte-identical to Ghidra memory at 0x521D4 (length 17). xrefs_to 0x521D4 = only READ + DATA from fd2_chapter_18_end (single reader, no writers) -> const confirmed. Disassembly at 0x23CFE/0x23D03/0x23D05 confirms MOVSD x4 + MOVSB (16+1=17 byte copy). Consumer fd2_setup_chars_and_camera_for_intro (0x233C6) confirms one-byte-per-char indexed read into runtime_char.bPos_y. Existing src comment block (chtab2.c lines 165-177) was already accurate and concise -> kept, no src edit. Ghidra data plate was blank (<null>, as were both sibling tables) -> created a concise PLATE_COMMENT consistent with the verified src understanding. Only the shard file is staged for this symbol's commit since chtab2.c was unchanged.
